questions.q: On a sailing ship, the “lubber’s hole” is ___.
questions.a: a gap in the mast platform for nervous climbers
alts: a hole in the crows nest floor
a hole in the platform at the top of the mast
decoys: where the cook throws the scraps
the gap under the captain’s door
questions.fact: Proper sailors climbed round the outside of the platform. Landlubbers sneaked up through the hole.

questions.q: An “Irish pennant” is ___.
questions.a: a loose rope end left flapping about
decoys: a green flag flown on Sundays
a tot of whiskey before breakfast
questions.fact: A sign of a scruffy ship, and an easy way to get shouted at by the bosun.

questions.q: On an old warship, the “loblolly boy” was ___.
decoys: the lad who fed the chickens
questions.fact: Named after loblolly, a thick porridge he dished out to the sick and wounded.

questions.q: A “bumboat” is ___.
questions.a: a little boat that sells goods to ships at anchor
alts: a boat selling supplies to ships
questions.fact: They’d paddle out with fruit, drink and souvenirs for sailors who weren’t allowed ashore.

questions.q: A “monkey’s fist” is ___.
questions.a: a ball-shaped knot that weights the end of a throwing line
alts: a heavy knot on the end of a rope
decoys: a bunch of bananas kept for luck
questions.fact: Heavy enough to throw a rope across to the dock. Sneaky sailors hid a stone inside.

questions.q: To “swallow the anchor” means ___.
questions.a: to retire from the sea and settle ashore
decoys: to down a pint in one
to lose a bet with the captain

questions.q: “Baggywrinkle” is ___.
questions.a: fluffy old rope wrapped round rigging to stop sails rubbing
decoys: a sailor’s wrinkled hands after a wash
a pudding made from leftover biscuits
questions.fact: It looks like giant hairy caterpillars clinging to the ropes.

questions.q: In old sailors’ slang, “cackle fruit” were ___.
Fiddler’s Green is ___.
questions.a: a sailors’ heaven of endless rum, music and dancing
decoys: the patch of deck where the band played
the green slime on the bottom of a hull

questions.q: A “holystone” was ___.
questions.a: a soft sandstone used to scrub the decks
alts: a stone for scrubbing the deck
decoys: a lucky pebble kept in the captain’s pocket
a gravestone for sailors buried at sea
questions.fact: Sailors scrubbed on their knees, as if at prayer. Hence holy.

questions.q: A “bosun’s chair” is ___.
questions.a: a plank on a rope, for hoisting someone up the mast
alts: a seat hung from a rope
a swing for working up the mast
decoys: the only comfy chair on board
a punishment for falling asleep on watch

questions.q: “Chock-a-block” first meant ___.
questions.a: two pulley blocks hauled so tight together they can’t move
decoys: a hold stacked to the ceiling with cargo
a cannon jammed with too much powder
a harbour too full to moor in

questions.q: On a sailing ship, a “sheet” is not a sail. It’s ___.
alts: a rope that controls a sail
questions.fact: Let the sheets fly loose and the ship staggers about. Hence three sheets to the wind.

questions.q: A “slush fund” was first ___.
questions.a: money from selling the fat skimmed off the ship’s cooking
decoys: money hidden in the bilge water
a bribe for the harbour master

questions.q: “Batten down the hatches”: battens are ___.
questions.a: strips of wood that pin covers over the hatches
decoys: iron bolts the size of your arm

questions.q: “Starboard” comes from the Old English “steorbord”, meaning ___.
questions.fact: Ships were steered with an oar on the right, so they moored on the left: the side by the port.

questions.q: The left side of a ship was renamed “port” because the old name, “larboard”, ___.
decoys: was a rude word in Portuguese
was the name of a hated admiral
was too hard to shout in a storm

questions.q: Grog, sailors’ watered-down rum, is named after an admiral’s nickname, which came from his ___.
decoys: habit of falling asleep at dinner
questions.fact: Admiral Vernon, “Old Grog”, watered down the rum in 1740. His sailors were not grateful.

questions.q: Old sailors would never whistle on board, because it was said to ___.
A sailor with a swallow tattoo was showing off that he had ___.
questions.fact: Swallows come home every year, so it was also a promise to make it back.

questions.q: Some sailors had a pig and a hen tattooed on their feet to ___.
decoys: make sure they were always fed
questions.fact: Pigs and hens were carried in wooden crates, which floated free when a ship went down.

questions.q: In 1493, Christopher Columbus reported seeing three mermaids, and noted that they ___.
questions.a: weren’t as pretty as they’re painted
alts: were not as beautiful as people said
questions.fact: He’d almost certainly spotted manatees.

questions.q: To look terrifying in battle, Blackbeard would tuck ___ under his hat.
questions.fact: They wreathed his face in smoke. Very effective. Smelt awful.

questions.q: Under Black Bart Roberts’ pirate code, anyone still drinking after 8pm had to ___.
questions.a: do it out on the open deck
decoys: sing for the rest of the crew
questions.fact: Lights and candles went out at eight. The code was surprisingly big on bedtimes.

questions.q: Black Bart Roberts’ pirate code also said the ship’s musicians got ___.
decoys: the first pick of any loot
to sleep in the captain’s cabin
questions.fact: The other six days and nights, they played on request.

questions.q: When Captain Kidd was hanged at Wapping in 1701, ___.
questions.a: the rope snapped, so they hanged him twice
decoys: the crowd cheered for an encore
he asked for a cup of tea first
questions.fact: His body was then tarred and hung in a cage by the Thames for years, as a warning to sailors.

questions.q: The Welsh privateer Henry Morgan, who’s now on a rum bottle, ended his days as ___.
decoys: the landlord of a London tavern

questions.q: The Spanish called Sir Francis Drake “El Draque”, which means ___.
One theory says the pirate flag’s name, the Jolly Roger, comes from the French “joli rouge”, meaning ___.
questions.fact: Early pirate flags were often red, meaning no mercy would be shown.

questions.q: One theory says pirates wore eye patches so they could ___.
questions.a: keep one eye used to the dark below deck
alts: keep one eye adjusted to darkness
decoys: hide a missing eye from their mums
sleep on watch without being caught
questions.fact: Swap the patch to the other eye when you head below, and you can see straight away.

questions.q: Robert Louis Stevenson drew the first map of Treasure Island to entertain ___.
decoys: the landlady of a Scottish inn
questions.fact: It was a rainy holiday in Braemar. The boy asked for a story to go with it.

questions.q: In Treasure Island, Long John Silver’s parrot is called ___.
questions.fact: Named after Silver’s old captain. She squawks “Pieces of eight!”

questions.q: Nelson’s body was brought home from Trafalgar preserved in a barrel of ___.
questions.fact: Legend says the sailors drank some of it on the way. They called it tapping the admiral.

questions.q: Black Tot Day, 31 July 1970, was the day the Royal Navy ___.
questions.a: stopped giving sailors a daily rum ration
alts: stopped the daily tot of rum
questions.fact: Sailors held mock funerals. Some wore black armbands.

questions.q: The Royal Navy’s old toast for Saturday night is “Our wives and sweethearts…” and it ends ___.
decoys: and the ship that brings us home

questions.q: Henry VIII’s warship, the Mary Rose, sank in 1545 ___.
questions.a: right in front of Henry, who was watching from the shore
decoys: on its first day afloat, before leaving the harbour
because the cook set fire to it
questions.fact: Divers later found the skeleton of the ship’s dog, Hatch, in the wreck.

questions.q: The kids’ TV show Blue Peter is named after a flag that ships fly to say ___.
questions.fact: A blue flag with a white square in the middle. The show was a voyage of adventure.

questions.q: In 2002, the Shipping Forecast sea area Finisterre was renamed ___.
questions.fact: After Robert FitzRoy, founder of the Met Office, who also captained Darwin’s ship, the Beagle.

questions.q: The Plimsoll line painted on a ship’s hull shows ___.
questions.a: how heavily it can safely be loaded
alts: how much cargo it can carry
decoys: where the barnacles should be scraped to
the height of the highest wave it’s survived
where to paint the ship’s name

questions.q: In 1859 Britain and the USA nearly went to war over ___.
questions.fact: An American farmer shot a British pig eating his potatoes. The only casualty was the pig.

questions.q: In England, every unmarked mute swan on open water technically belongs to ___.
Legend says that if the ravens ever leave the Tower of London, ___.
decoys: it will rain for forty days
questions.fact: They keep at least six. Plus a spare.

questions.q: A group of sharks is called a ___.
A group of jellyfish is called a ___.
A baby oyster is called a ___.
A seahorse is unusual because it’s the ___ who gives birth.
